activities.anchor: the map of age has split in two
activities.caption: drag the divider — the two halves of the age map
activities.name: pmAgeMapCompare

config.prompt: One planet, two demographic halves — drag the divider:

before.label: The shrinking half
before.text: Japan, Italy and South Korea: shrinking and ageing, fertility long below replacement.

after.label: The young half
after.text: Africa's median age remains about 19 — the workforce of the century is being born now.

config.why: Migration — always contested, always constant — is the hinge connecting the halves: young regions, ageing regions, and the flows between them.

config.prompt: The world's annual population increase today is roughly how many million people?
config.why: Roughly 70 million — the rate crested above 2% a year in the early 1960s and has fallen under 1%; the annual increase peaked near 90 million in the late 1980s. In April 2023 India passed China — not because India grew faster that year, but because China's fertility collapsed below replacement decades ago.

activities.caption: true or false — stock versus speed
activities.name: pmLevelJudge

statements.s: The absolute number of people has never been higher.
statements.why: About 8.2 billion in 2024 — the stock is still rising even as the speed falls.

statements.s: The world's growth rate peaked in the 1960s and has more than halved since.
statements.why: It crested above 2% a year in the early 1960s and now runs under 1%.

statements.s: A big total means a quick doubling — the two always travel together.
statements.why: One is a stock, the other a speed — mixing them up inverts the real policy problem, which is now as much about shrinking and ageing as about boom.

statements.s: Birth rates take generations to follow death rates down.
statements.why: Deaths can fall in a decade — clean water, vaccination, antibiotics — while births are bound up with women's education, urbanisation, child survival and income.

activities.anchor: The arithmetic is worth doing by hand at least once
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the demographer's note
activities.name: pmDecreeSpot

config.prompt: One line of this demographer's note is wrong — click it:
lines: A crude birth rate of 28 and a crude death rate of 8 gives natural increase of 20 per 1,000 — 2.0% a year.
The rule of 70 converts that to a doubling in about 35 years, before any migration is counted.
A country with birth rate 9 and death rate 11 is already shrinking by 0.2% a year — roughly a fifth of its people in a century.
China's pro-natalist three-child policy (2021) has so far moved fertility substantially upward.
Romania's 1966 Decree 770 produced a birth spike, a surge of unsafe abortions and a cohort of institutionalised children.
config.correction: China's three-child policy has so far moved fertility barely at all — decrees cannot outmuscle the social forces behind fertility.
config.why: Birth rates fall reliably with girls' education, child survival, urbanisation and access to contraception — the 'empowerment route' the transition model quietly encodes; France's sustained family policy reaches about 1.6, Europe's highest, still far from replacement.

activities.anchor: A wide base (Niger, DR Congo) means
activities.caption: pin the barrel pyramid on the transition ladder
activities.name: pmStagePlace

config.prompt: A barrel-shaped pyramid (Brazil, Mexico) sits at which stage of the demographic transition?
config.why: Barrel means mid-walk — birth rates falling as urbanisation and education spread; the pyramid's shape is the transition drawn as a silhouette, a photograph of the past with its future attached.

activities.caption: file each flow under its factor
activities.name: pmPushPullSort

config.prompt: Push, pull, obstacle, person — file each fact:

items.label: wages, safety, education, family already there
visas, deserts, seas, the price of a smuggler
who is free and able to move — the young, the skilled, the connected
the nearly 8 million Venezuelans who left after 2015 — a collapse-of-order flow
the Mexico–US corridor of around 11 million — a wage-gradient flow

config.why: Internal migration dwarfs it all: China's floating population of rural workers is around 370 million — more than all the world's international migrants combined (281 million, 3.6% of humanity).

activities.anchor: remittance arithmetic deserves a worked example
activities.caption: call the corridor's annual flow
activities.name: pmRemitEstimate

config.prompt: A construction worker in Dubai sends home $200 a month. One million such workers — smaller than several real corridors — move how much per year?
config.why: $2.4 billion a year — rivalling a ministry's entire capital budget, delivered without conditions, advisors or overhead; multiplied across the global system it becomes the $650-billion-plus flow to low- and middle-income countries, with the Philippines' share worth about 8.5% of its GDP.

activities.anchor: the data show the neighbouring country
activities.caption: bet on the direction of most migration
activities.name: pmSouthPredict

config.q: Most international migrants move from poor countries to rich ones. True or false — and what actually dominates?
choices: True — the wealthy-world border is where the flows are
False — most international migration is South–South, and internal migration dwarfs everything
False — most migration is refugee movement between continents
config.why: A Kenyan worker in Tanzania, a Burkinaabé farmer in Côte d'Ivoire — and China's internal floating population alone tops all international migrants combined. The wealthy-world border gets the coverage; the statistics say otherwise.
